ov: A domesticated member of the horse family, bred from the African wild ass some 5,000–7,000 years ago and used mainly as a working animal ever since. There are more than 40 million donkeys worldwide.

why.et: A few donkeys are raised for meat or milk; about 3.5 million donkeys and mules are slaughtered for meat each year.

ht: Under 90 cm to about 150 cm at the shoulder
rg: Worldwide, mostly in developing countries as working animals; adapted to marginal desert land.

cf.tip: A mule is a cross between a male donkey and a female horse. The rarer hinny is the reverse.
A donkey has much larger ears, which help it pick up distant sounds and cool its blood.

fx: In prosperous countries a donkey can live 30–50 years, but working donkeys in the poorest countries often live only 12–15.
